## Overview

The Chugach, also known as Chugach Sugpiaq or Chugachigmiut, are an Alaska Native people of the Kenai Peninsula and Prince William Sound on the southern coast of Alaska. They are an Alutiiq (Pacific Native) people who speak the Chugach dialect of the Alutiiq language. Their villages include Chenega Bay, Eyak, Nanwalek (English Bay), Port Graham, and Tatitlek. The Chugach have lived around Prince William Sound for millennia, according to archaeological finds, and encountered the Russian explorer Vitus Bering in 1741.

## Festivals & rituals

The sources do record historical accounts of androgynous third-gender or two-spirit individuals known as *aranu'tiq*. Anthropologists writing in the 1950s described these individuals as being considered male on one side of their bodies and female on the other. Some had descriptive names such as “Tyakutyik,” translated as “What Kind Of People Are These Two?”, although the description was given to many types of people in the community and was not related to gender expression.

## Foodways

The sources state that the Chugach economy was based on fishing and that it was badly affected by environmental damage caused by the Exxon Valdez oil spill in 1989.

## Language & religion

Chugach people speak one of two dialects of the Pacific Gulf Yupik language; the other is Koniag. These Central Yupik languages belong to the Alaskan Yupik language family. The language was once written in Cyrillic script and is now written in the Latin script.

commons_photos.description:
Exhibit in the Arvid Adolf Etholén collection, Museum of Cultures, Helsinki, Finland. Photography was permitted in the museum without restriction. Spruce root hat. The crown is on close plain twining, the sturdier raised twining on the brim forms a whirl pattern. The brim is finished with braiding painted in reddish brown. The hat is painted blue-green all over, with an unidentified imitation of Tlingit totemic design in yellow, red and black on the crown. The edge of the brim, the “seam” between the brim and the crown, and the crown are decorated with clusters of white, red, blue and black glass beads, also used to accentuate the groups of dentalia covering the hat. Two black velvet ribbons lined and trimmed with cotton fabric are sewn to the hoop inside the hat and stitched together under the chin. At the ears, they are hung with pendants comprising 12 dentalia and glass beads.
This hat is probably the one spruce root hat documented as Chugach Eskimo in the Etholén collection of 1846. Holmberg (1855) mentions that in 1850 the Koniag reserved their old spruce root hats for kayak trips; otherwise they had already started to wear (European-style) visor caps. The decoration of trade beads and dentalia, the coloring and the design which differs from Tlingit formline painting show that this valuable hat is of Alutiiq origin, as confirmed also by Holm (1995) who further thinks it might be specifically from Kodiak Island.
